prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Create one portrait anime wardrobe STYLE GUIDE, with a full-body fashion avatar and legible inline annotations. Character inspiration: Kaneki (Tokyo Ghoul). SOURCE CHARACTER PALETTE (authoritative): Primary: Jet Black | Secondary: Stark White | Accent: Deep Plum / Purple | Pop: Blood Red. Preserve the primary color prominently; do not replace it with a neutral top. The outfit is an everyday casual reinterpretation, not cosplay. Adult male avatar inspired by Kirito / Sung Jinwoo, 172 cm tall, compact natural proportions, about 6.5 to 7 heads tall, normal legs, lean average build, friendly confident face. Clearly UPRIGHT SPIKY BLACK HAIR with pointed tufts sticking UP, no floppy fringe. EXACT gym OUTFIT: Plain black relaxed short-sleeve athletic training tee; Plain white seven-inch training shorts, no stripes; Plain black supportive training shoes; Simple plum sports watch. Each garment is ONE PLAIN SOLID COLOR, readily available basics. NO contrasting panels, contrasting collars or sleeves, stripes, gradients, logos, prints, weapons or fantasy armor. Keep the signature color combination across separate pieces. Simple TV-anime clean ink outlines and FLAT SOLID FILLS, minimal hard-edged cel shading, no realism, texture rendering or glossy gradients. White/off-white background. Full body including every hair tip and both complete shoes, with head and foot margins. Subject takes about 60 percent of canvas width. A polished minimalist fashion reference sheet with generous side gutters, thin leader lines pointing to the relevant garment or accessory, and a compact color-swatch legend. Clearly typeset LARGE, HIGH-CONTRAST dark text, readable when zoomed on a phone; use short labels, never tiny paragraphs. Title exact: "Kaneki / GYM / 03". Required callouts verbatim: "BLACK FIRST"; "WHITE CONTRAST"; "PLUM ACCENT"; "FREE MOVEMENT"; "BRANDING: SMALL TONAL MARKS ONLY"; "172 CM / EVERYDAY FIT". Place color callouts next to their actual matching pieces; if a contrast is only in the legend, do not falsely point at an unrelated piece. Place branding guidance below the figure, with a small empty chest-mark outline example OUTSIDE the clothes (not a real logo). Do not actually add branding to the clothes. Keep the body anatomy and casual clothing as important as the clear notes. Flat, restrained, readable editorial layout. Single portrait, no multiple figures.
